weighting: Each family receives equal weight within its SEP group.
estimand: Distribution across families of model-predicted expected school value added, in normalized VA standard deviations.
curveMethod: Published kernel density estimates; baseline bandwidth held fixed across scenarios within each SEP group.
policyControlScope: These published experiment-sample figures are selected independently from the population policy controls. No distributions for partial take-up, targeted treatment, or cost sensitivities are inferred from population means.

figures.label: Baseline inequality
figures.title: Baseline differences in expected school value added
figures.caption: No intervention. The two curves compare SEP and non-SEP families; vertical lines mark group means.
figures.alt: Baseline expected school value-added densities: SEP families have a mean of 0.19 SD and non-SEP families 0.47 SD, a gap of 0.28 SD.
figures.summary: Baseline mean expected VA is 0.19 SD for SEP families and 0.47 SD for non-SEP families.
figures.assumptions: No intervention · school conditions held fixed

figures.label: Demand response
figures.title: Full information: demand response
figures.caption: Solid lines show no treatment; dashed lines show full treatment with school quality and prices fixed. SEP families appear above non-SEP families. Vertical lines mark group means.
figures.alt: Expected VA distributions shift right under full treatment. The paper reports a mean increase of 0.225 SD for SEP families and 0.167 SD for non-SEP families.
figures.summary: The paper reports gains of 0.225 SD for SEP families and 0.167 SD for non-SEP families in this sample.
figures.assumptions: 100% take-up among eligible families · fixed quality and prices · no capacity constraints

figures.label: Capacity constraints
figures.title: Full information with capacity constraints
figures.caption: Gray solid lines show no treatment; gray dashed lines show full treatment under free choice; colored solid lines add deferred acceptance with capacity constraints. SEP families appear above non-SEP families.
figures.alt: Baseline, demand-only, and capacity-constrained expected VA distributions. With capacity constraints, the mean gain is 0.134 SD for SEP families and 0.092 SD for non-SEP families.
figures.summary: With limited seats, the gains are 0.134 SD for SEP families and 0.092 SD for non-SEP families in this sample.
figures.assumptions: 100% take-up among eligible families · capacity-constrained assignment · fixed school quality

figures.label: School-quality response
figures.title: Full information with capacity constraints and school responses
figures.caption: Gray solid lines show no treatment; gray dashed lines show full treatment with free choice and fixed quality; colored solid lines add capacity-constrained assignment and private-school quality responses. SEP families appear above non-SEP families.
figures.alt: Baseline, demand-only, and equilibrium expected VA distributions. With capacity constraints and school-quality responses, the mean gain is 0.257 SD for SEP families and 0.208 SD for non-SEP families.
figures.summary: Allowing private-school quality to respond produces gains of 0.257 SD for SEP families and 0.208 SD for non-SEP families in this sample.
figures.assumptions: 100% take-up among eligible families · capacity constraints · private-school quality response · public-school quality fixed
